schedule: Students will meet with me for at least three group meetings. (Students may make individual appointments with me as needed.) A week before these group meetings students will have submitted their drafts to me and one another for peer review, and we will discuss the peer reviews at the meetings.
scorePolicy:
Students will write three senior project drafts, one of five pages, one of ten pages, and one of fifteen pages and will write useful peer reviews for one another.

In the springs semester, the final grade is based predominantly on effort and participation (but partially still on writing results). The excellent student will

1) Set deadlines and meet those deadlines.

2) Meet the length requirement for drafts.

3) Stay in communication with me and keep me updated on the progress of the draft, any challenges, etc.

4) Take the time to give useful feedback to group members and work well with other group members.

5) Take feedback seriously and work to improve from draft to draft (This is even more important than meeting the length requirement.)

6) Show the ability to stay strong through obstacles and frustrations in order to write a strong project (and talk to me early if you are having trouble).

7) Have a strong direction for the paper, in which they are in conversation with interesting outside sources and yet making original, debatable, and clear claims, which they support with analyzed evidence.

8) Follow the rules and conventions for academic honesty, including citation rules and making sure all ideas are their original ideas, thought up independently.

Students who do all of the above will do well in the spring semester. Points will be taken off as needed for problems, but students are encouraged, if they make a mistake an any area, to be in clear communication with me about the mistake and just to fix the mistake as soon as possible. The one major issue students need to watch out for is plagiarism as failures in citation and/or AI writing could lead students to receive a zero. Students should make sure they understand these expectations and cite appropriately.
